descriptionChirho: To bring a work, speech, or activity to its intended conclusion; transitive completion of a defined task (Arabic akmala/faraġa, Korean 마쳤다/끝냈다, Swahili -maliza/-kamilisha).
To bring people or things to utter destruction; annihilative consumption, often of God's wrath against enemies (Arabic afnā/yufnī, Korean 멸하다/멸망시키다, Swahili -angamiza/-teketeza).
To reach a natural end, be finished, or run out; intransitive cessation or completion of a process, supply, or period (Arabic faniya/intahā/nafida, Korean 끝났다/없어지다, Swahili -isha/-kwisha/-malizika).
To become exhausted or faint, especially of eyes, strength, or soul failing from grief, longing, or weariness (Arabic kallat/iḍmaḥallat, Korean 쇠하다/마르다, Swahili -choka/-shindwa/-zimia).
To be settled or decided as a judicial or divine decree, a specialized usage where completion takes on the sense of finality of a decision (Arabic quḍiyat, Korean 결정되었다, Swahili -amuliwa).
Passive of the Piel: to be brought to completion by an external agent; the work is finished upon the subject (Arabic uktumilat/intahat, Korean 완성되었다/끝났다, Swahili -kamilika/-malizika).
To pine or yearn intensely, a rare specialized sense where the consuming is emotional desire rather than physical destruction (Arabic wātaqat, Korean 사모했다, Swahili -tamani).
To consume by eating or devouring, a concrete metabolic sense distinct from abstract destruction (Arabic ya'kulu, Korean 먹어치우다, Swahili -kula).
To bring a purpose, prophecy, or divine plan to fruition; intransitive fulfillment with teleological completion (Arabic itmām, Korean 완성하다/성취하다, Swahili -timiza/-timia).
To use up resources such as arrows, days, or provisions; the consuming is depletion of a supply rather than destruction of persons (Arabic atimmu, Korean 다하다/소모하다, Swahili -tumia).
The abstract noun form denoting the state or act of destruction/annihilation (Arabic fanā', Korean 멸망, Swahili uharibifu).
